body:
Conclusion: the integration should expect a fail-closed `InvalidCursorError` (Ordarium `code === "INVALID_CURSOR"`). It is not `LEDGER_CORRUPT` (damaged ledger), not a silent restart from the beginning of the feed, not `LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED` (that guard fires only when the ledger lacks the feed capability), and not `STATE_REVISION_CONFLICT` (that is the state-CAS write path). Map it by `instanceof`/code, not by a hard-coded number.

The two local records contradict each other: docs/engineering/09-error-contract-a.md says the cursor-rejection contract is **global** (one position shared by all readers), 09-error-contract-b.md says it is **per-consumer** (each consumer holds its own position). Both claim "normative, current scope", carry no dates, no supersession, no author, and neither is indexed in docs/engineering/README.md, so neither record has a local precedence rule over the other. The conflict is settled by a stronger, version-scoped local source: the pinned dependency the integration actually runs.

Evidence (pinned Ordarium v1.3.1 — package.json pins the 1.3.1 tarballs; node_modules/@ordarium/{core,ledger-sqlite}/package.json report 1.3.1):
- node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/errors.d.ts (`InvalidCursorError`): "A caller-supplied change-feed cursor could not be decoded as a durable position (ORD-BOOT-0). Distinct from LEDGER_CORRUPT: this is invalid caller input, not damaged ledger content, and it fails closed instead of silently restarting from the beginning of the feed." errors.js constructs code `INVALID_CURSOR` with message "The change cursor is not a valid durable position; refusing to guess a resume point".
- core/dist/src/ledger.js `decodeStateChangeCursor()` throws `InvalidCursorError` for any non-`{c:"<digits>"}` payload, and `MemoryLedger.changes()` throws it when `after > this.#stateChanges.length` ("a position beyond the highest known commit ... signals a foreign/restored/corrupt cursor and must fail closed").
- ledger-sqlite/dist/src/index.js `SqliteLedger.changes()` (lines ~383-393): validates the decoded position against `#stateChangeHighWater()`, implemented at line 580 as `SELECT MAX(change_seq) FROM ordarium_state_changes` — a **ledger-wide**, not per-namespace, high-water mark; if `after` exceeds it, `throw new InvalidCursorError()`. The in-code comment is explicit: "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence ... Concurrent commits only raise the mark, so a valid cursor cannot be falsely rejected; a restored/replaced ledger lowers it and fails closed."
- core/dist/src/types.d.ts confirms both points: `StateChangePage.cursor` is "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change", and `StateChangeFilter.namespace` only "Restrict[s] observation to one namespace".

Decision: Record A (global position) is the operative reading; Record B is contradicted by the pinned implementation and, if adopted, would falsely reject valid stored cursors (a global change position can legitimately exceed a single namespace's last sequence). So a rejected stored observation cursor is a fail-closed `INVALID_CURSOR`, and the integration must treat it as an invalid durable resume point rather than resynchronising or retrying from zero.

Scope note: this concerns the change-feed/observation cursor (`StateChangePage.cursor`, from `SqliteLedger.changes()`/`MemoryLedger.changes()`), which is the durable resume position meant to be stored. It is not the `nextCursor` pagination cursor of `listStates` — the only cursor the workspace stores today (src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts:66-70), which is a different surface that throws `TypeError` on malformed input. The workspace's `src/` has zero calls to `changes()` today, so this is the failure to expect when the change feed is consumed.

Peers: no contact needed. The question is decidable from version-scoped local provenance alone (pinned 1.3.1 artifacts), and the peer-inbox is empty; the peer owns Ordarium's contract text, but the artifact already fixes the runtime behaviour the workspace's integration will observe. The actionable local follow-up is to delete/correct the orphaned Record B so the two records stop contradicting each other.

Conclusion: the integration should expect a fail-closed InvalidCursorError (code INVALID_CURSOR) when a stored change-feed/observation cursor is rejected; the operative semantics is the global one (Record A), not per-consumer (Record B).

Basis: pinned Ordarium v1.3.1 (package.json pins the ordarium-v1.3.1 tarballs; node_modules reports 1.3.1). errors.d.ts/js define InvalidCursorError/"INVALID_CURSOR" for a caller-supplied change-feed cursor that is not a valid durable position, explicitly distinct from LEDGER_CORRUPT and explicitly refusing to restart the feed. SqliteLedger.changes() validates the decoded position against the ledger-wide high-water mark (SELECT MAX(change_seq) FROM ordarium_state_changes) and MemoryLedger.changes() against total commits, both refusing to compare against the requested namespace's last sequence — i.e. the position is global/filter-independent, and a valid cursor cannot be falsely rejected by a namespace filter. StateChangePage.cursor is documented as the "opaque, filter-independent durable position".

Boundary handling: because docs/engineering/09-error-contract-a.md (global) and 09-error-contract-b.md (per-consumer) are equally normative with no local supersession, I opened thread thr_1369075b-e17a-4cf7-83f6-16fa65c23ed8 and BoundaryContract cursor-rejection-error-contract (basis evt_d73a2bf6, revision 2, termsDigest a13ec6a973e966e3d753135a68eb6eb6f68a1cdb0cad98a55c4411b6185d9810) to ordarium.main, which owns ORD-BOOT-0 and docs/12–17, and accepted it on the Palimpsest side (evt_aee8d575, evt_f3f5fe15). The peer has not yet accepted or answered; if its docs/12–17 disagree with the pinned behaviour, the failure class must be taken from that authoritative answer instead.

Peers: no further action possible from Palimpsest-local evidence; confirming the contract revision with ordarium.main closes the boundary.

Cannot legitimately determine it yet — the proposition is blocked on an unresolved authority boundary, not on missing local evidence.

Why it is unresolved:
- The workspace holds two competing, equally normative "current scope" records with no local tie-break: docs/engineering/09-error-contract-a.md (cursor-rejection contract is global — one position shared by all readers) and 09-error-contract-b.md (per-consumer — each consumer holds its own position). Neither is dated, superseded, or indexed in docs/engineering/README.md; the alignment charter (07-ordarium-alignment.md) assigns the Ordarium error/change-feed contract to Ordarium's own docs/12–17, so Palimpsest has no in-domain precedence rule.
- The strongest local evidence points one way but is not authoritative: pinned Ordarium v1.3.1 (package.json tarball pins; node_modules reports 1.3.1) defines InvalidCursorError with code INVALID_CURSOR for a caller-supplied change-feed cursor that is not a valid durable position, explicitly distinct from LEDGER_CORRUPT and explicitly fail-closed ("refusing to guess a resume point"). SqliteLedger.changes() validates the decoded position against the ledger-wide high-water mark (SELECT MAX(change_seq) FROM ordarium_state_changes) and MemoryLedger.changes() against total commits, both explicitly refusing to compare against the requested namespace's last sequence; StateChangePage.cursor is documented as the "opaque, filter-independent durable position". So the evidence-supported candidate is: global semantics, and a rejected stored observation cursor yields a fail-closed InvalidCursorError (INVALID_CURSOR) — not per-consumer rejection, not LEDGER_CORRUPT, not a silent restart. But this is inference from the pinned dist artifact, and the authority owner must confirm it against docs/12–17.
- I sought that authority: thread thr_1369075b-e17a-4cf7-83f6-16fa65c23ed8 (question evt_d73a2bf6, blocking need evt_aee8d575, proposal evt_f3f5fe15) and BoundaryContract cursor-rejection-error-contract@2 (termsDigest a13ec6a973e966e3d753135a68eb6eb6f68a1cdb0cad98a55c4411b6185d9810, accepted on the Palimpsest side, basis evt_d73a2bf6). ordarium.main has not responded or accepted, and the decision policy has twice blocked a resolved disposition for this proposition as lacking an accepted authority-participation basis (ticket now CONSULTING).

Disposition: unresolved. The integration cannot yet be told authoritatively which failure to expect; the pending but strong candidate is InvalidCursorError / INVALID_CURSOR (fail-closed, global position).

Path to resolution (owned by ordarium.main): accept cursor-rejection-error-contract@2 or propose corrected terms answering (1) global vs per-consumer position semantics, (2) the exact failure class/code for a rejected stored observation cursor on the v1.3.1 line, and (3) whether a valid stored cursor can be falsely rejected when a namespace filter is supplied.
